# 📦 Contributing to Bert XV

Here is a guide to get started contributing to Bert XV.

## 🐛 Reporting Bugs

If you spot a bug in any code, please create a GitHub issue on the Bert XV repository and include as much detail as possible. Make sure to include the following:

- A clear and descriptive title.
- Steps to reproduce the issue.
- Expected behaviour and what actually happens.
- Any relevant logs and/or screenshots.
- Any other additional details that you think should be included.

[Submit a bug](https://github.com/FRC-4750-Bishop-Eustace/Bert-XV/issues/new?template=BUG-REPORT.yml)

## 💡 Suggesting Features

Feature requests are appreciated!

Notify any collaborators to get editor access or to push requests.

## ⚒️ Contributing Code

### 🚀 Getting Started

### ↕️ Pull Request Guidelines

- Follow the coding style of the project.
- Write clear and descriptive comments and commit messages.
- Ensure that your code passes all tests and is bug-free before submission.

[Submit a pull request](https://github.com/FRC-4750-Bishop-Eustace/Bert-XV/pull/new)

## 🛠️ Setting Up the development enviroment

### 🧰 Prerequisites

1. Install [**Git**](https://git-scm.com/install/)
2. Install [**Python**](https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3147/)
3. Install [**FRC & WPILib tools**](https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/zero-to-robot/step-2/frc-game-tools.html) (including the RoboRIO and/or SystemCore toolchain)
4. Install [**RobotPy**](https://robotpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/)

### ⚙️ Installation

1. Clone the Bert XV repository.
2. Navigate to the projects directory.
3. Install dependencies (if required).

### ▶️ Testing and Running your project

1. Navigate to the repo directory.
2. Run the `robotpy` CL tool after making any changes:
  - Installation
  ```sh
  robotpy sync
  ```
  - Building
  ```sh
  robotpy run
  ```
  - Testing
  ```sh
  robotpy test --builtin
  ```
  - Simulation
  ```sh
  robotpy sim
  ```
  - Deploying
  ```sh
  robotpy deploy
  ```
